passages.title: 台灣米其林指南 2025
passages.text: On August 19, 2025, the Michelin Guide Taiwan 2025 was announced. This year, 53 {1} in Taiwan received Michelin stars, and eight of them got stars for the first time. The guide covers cities such as Taipei, Taichung, Tainan, and Kaohsiung. It also lists cheaper places that serve good food at fair prices, from beef noodle shops to small family {2} and even a local {3}. Many tourists now use the guide to plan their meals in Taiwan. After the news came out, my uncle took my family to a small shop in Tainan that was on the list. We waited in line for an hour, but the rice noodles were amazing. Next door, there was an old {4}, so my sister and I read comic books while we waited. My uncle said he would save money in the {5} so we could try a starred restaurant next year.

blanks.why: 53 restaurants received stars「53 家餐廳獲得星星」。spoons（湯匙）、coughs（咳嗽）、fevers（發燒）都不能得到米其林星星。
small family restaurants「小型家庭餐廳」。socks（襪子）、towels（毛巾）、lemons（檸檬）都不能供應食物。
a local bakery「一家當地的麵包店」，也被列在指南裡。fever、candle（蠟燭）、pumpkin（南瓜）都不是店家。
an old bookstore「一間老書店」，所以可以看漫畫。soup（湯）、cough、blanket（毯子）都不是能看書的地方。
save money in the bank「把錢存在銀行」。sugar（糖）、weather（天氣）、noise（噪音）都不能存錢。

passages.zh: 2025 年 8 月 19 日，《台灣米其林指南 2025》公布了。今年台灣有 53 家餐廳獲得米其林星級，其中 8 家是第一次摘星。指南涵蓋台北、台中、台南、高雄等城市，也列出許多價格合理又好吃的店，從牛肉麵店到小小的家庭餐廳，甚至還有一家當地麵包店。現在很多觀光客會用這本指南規劃在台灣的餐點。消息公布後，我舅舅帶我們全家去台南一家上榜的小店。我們排了一個小時，但米粉超好吃。隔壁有一間老書店，所以我和妹妹邊等邊看漫畫。舅舅說他會把錢存進銀行，明年帶我們去吃星級餐廳。

passages.title: 鬼滅之刃無限城篇的票房紀錄
passages.text: On July 18, 2025, the anime movie Demon Slayer: Infinity Castle opened in Japan. It broke the record for the biggest opening weekend in Japanese history. Later, it was shown in {1} around the world, and by November it had become the first Japanese film to earn more than 100 billion yen worldwide. In Taiwan, too, many fans went to see it again and again. Some movie {2} added early morning and late night shows because tickets sold out so fast. Near my home, a {3} even sold bread shaped like the main characters' faces, and a {4} gave a free drink to anyone who showed a movie ticket. My best friend and I saw it on the first day. Afterward, we went to a {5} to buy the comic books, but they were sold out, too!

blanks.why: shown in theaters around the world「在世界各地的戲院上映」。spoons（湯匙）、fevers（發燒）、lemons（檸檬）都不能放電影。
movie theaters added shows「電影院加開場次」。coughs（咳嗽）、towels（毛巾）、socks（襪子）都不能和 movie 組成場所。
a bakery sold bread「一家麵包店賣麵包」。pumpkin（南瓜）、cough、blanket（毯子）都不會賣麵包。
a restaurant gave a free drink「一家餐廳送免費飲料」。sugar（糖）、noise（噪音）、weather（天氣）都不能送飲料給客人。
went to a bookstore to buy comic books「去書店買漫畫」。candle（蠟燭）、sock（襪子）、fever 都不是賣書的地方。

passages.zh: 2025 年 7 月 18 日，動畫電影《鬼滅之刃 無限城篇》在日本上映，打破日本史上首映週末票房紀錄。後來它在世界各地的戲院上映，到了 11 月，成為第一部全球票房超過一千億日圓的日本電影。在台灣，很多粉絲也一看再看。有些電影院因為票賣得太快，加開了清晨和深夜場。我家附近有一家麵包店甚至賣主角臉形狀的麵包，還有一家餐廳只要出示電影票就送一杯飲料。我和最好的朋友在首映日就去看了。看完後，我們去書店想買漫畫，結果也賣光了！

passages.title: 爆紅的杜拜巧克力
passages.text: In 2024, a thick chocolate bar from Dubai became one of the most famous sweets on social media. It was first made by a small company called Fix Dessert Chocolatier. Inside the chocolate, there is a crunchy filling made of pistachio cream and kataifi, thin pieces of pastry. After a woman posted a video of herself eating it, the bar went viral, and people around the world wanted to try it. Soon, many {1} and dessert shops made their own versions. In Taiwan, some {2} even added "Dubai chocolate" desserts to their menus. The price of pistachios also went up because so many people wanted them. My aunt owns a small {3} in Taichung. Last year, she found a recipe in a cookbook from a {4} and made her own Dubai chocolate cookies. They sold out every day! She said she had to go to the {5} twice a week to put the money in.

blanks.why: many bakeries and dessert shops「很多麵包店和甜點店」。spoons（湯匙）、coughs（咳嗽）、fevers（發燒）都不會做甜點。
some restaurants added desserts to their menus「一些餐廳把甜點加進菜單」。socks（襪子）、lemons（檸檬）、towels（毛巾）都沒有菜單。
owns a small bakery「開了一家小麵包店」。soup（湯）、blanket（毯子）、candle（蠟燭）都不能「經營」來賣餅乾。
a cookbook from a bookstore「從書店買的食譜」。sugar（糖）、weather（天氣）、noise（噪音）都不賣書。
go to the bank to put the money in「去銀行存錢」。pumpkin（南瓜）、fever、sock 都不能存錢。

passages.zh: 2024 年，一款來自杜拜的厚巧克力成了社群媒體上最有名的甜點之一。它最早是由一家叫 Fix Dessert Chocolatier 的小公司做的。巧克力裡面包著酥脆的內餡，由開心果醬和細絲狀的酥皮做成。一位女性上傳自己吃它的影片後，這款巧克力爆紅，全世界的人都想吃。很快地，許多麵包店和甜點店都推出自己的版本。在台灣，有些餐廳甚至把「杜拜巧克力」甜點加進菜單。因為太多人想要，開心果的價格也跟著上漲。我阿姨在台中開了一家小麵包店。去年她從書店買的食譜書裡找到做法，做了自己的杜拜巧克力餅乾，每天都賣光！她說她一週得跑兩次銀行去存錢。

passages.title: 美國書店的逆轉勝
passages.text: For many years, people said that bookstores would disappear because of online shopping. But something surprising happened. In 2025, Barnes & Noble, the biggest {1} chain in the United States, planned to open about 60 new stores, even more than the year before. One big reason was BookTok, a part of TikTok where young people share books they love. When a book becomes popular there, readers rush to {2} to buy it. Many new stores also have cafés, so people can read and drink coffee at the same time. Some even have a small {3} inside. My cousin in California works at one. She says that on weekends, the store is as busy as a popular {4}. Last month, she sent me a book that everyone on BookTok was talking about. I read it in one night and then lent it to my friend, who said it was better than any movie at the {5}.

blanks.why: the biggest bookstore chain「最大的連鎖書店」。spoon（湯匙）、cough（咳嗽）、fever（發燒）都不能和 chain 組成連鎖店。
rush to bookstores to buy it「衝去書店買」。socks（襪子）、lemons（檸檬）、towels（毛巾）都不是買書的地方。
a small bakery inside「裡面有一間小麵包店」。soup（湯）、blanket（毯子）、candle（蠟燭）都不是店面。
as busy as a popular restaurant「跟熱門餐廳一樣忙」。sugar（糖）、noise（噪音）、weather（天氣）都不能用 popular … 比喻人潮。
better than any movie at the theater「比戲院裡任何電影都好看」。pumpkin（南瓜）、fever、sock 都不能放電影。

passages.zh: 多年來，大家都說書店會因為網路購物而消失。但令人驚訝的事發生了：2025 年，美國最大的連鎖書店邦諾書店計畫開設大約 60 家新店，比前一年還多。一個重要原因是 BookTok，也就是 TikTok 上年輕人分享喜愛書籍的社群。一本書在那裡爆紅時，讀者就會衝去書店買。很多新店還附設咖啡廳，讓人可以邊看書邊喝咖啡，有些甚至在店裡開了一間小麵包店。我住在加州的表姊在其中一家工作，她說週末店裡跟熱門餐廳一樣忙。上個月，她寄給我一本 BookTok 上大家都在討論的書。我一個晚上就看完了，再借給朋友，朋友說它比戲院裡任何電影都好看。

passages.title: 世界最佳餐廳在秘魯
passages.text: In June 2025, a restaurant called Maido in Lima, Peru, was named number one on a famous list of the world's 50 best {1}. Maido is run by chef Mitsuharu Tsumura, who has Japanese and Peruvian family roots. His food mixes Japanese cooking with ingredients from Peru, like fresh fish from the Pacific Ocean and corn and potatoes from the mountains. This style is called Nikkei cuisine. People in Peru were very proud, because Lima has many famous {2} and the city wants more visitors to come for its food. My aunt traveled to Lima two years ago. She said a dinner there cost a lot, so she took money out of the {3} before the trip. She also visited a small {4} near her hotel every morning for sweet bread. When she came home, she bought a Peruvian cookbook at a {5} and tried to cook for us. It was not the same, but we loved it anyway.

blanks.why: the world's 50 best restaurants「全世界 50 家最好的餐廳」，Maido 是餐廳。spoons（湯匙）、coughs（咳嗽）、fevers（發燒）都不能被評為最佳美食地點。
many famous restaurants「很多有名的餐廳」。socks（襪子）、lemons（檸檬）、towels（毛巾）都不能吸引人來吃。
took money out of the bank「從銀行領錢」。soup（湯）、cough（咳嗽）、blanket（毯子）都不能領錢。
a small bakery for sweet bread「一家賣甜麵包的小麵包店」。sugar（糖）、noise（噪音）、weather（天氣）都不是店。
bought a cookbook at a bookstore「在書店買食譜」。candle（蠟燭）、pumpkin（南瓜）、fever 都不賣書。

passages.zh: 2025 年 6 月，秘魯利馬一家叫 Maido 的餐廳在「世界 50 最佳餐廳」榜單上獲選第一名。Maido 由主廚津村光晴經營，他有日本和秘魯的血統。他的料理把日本烹調手法和秘魯食材結合在一起，例如太平洋的新鮮海魚，以及山區的玉米和馬鈴薯，這種風格叫做「日秘料理」。秘魯人非常驕傲，因為利馬有很多有名的餐廳，這座城市也希望有更多遊客為了美食而來。我阿姨兩年前去過利馬。她說那裡的一頓晚餐很貴，所以出發前先從銀行領了錢。她每天早上也會去飯店附近一家小麵包店買甜麵包。回國後，她在書店買了一本秘魯食譜，試著煮給我們吃。雖然味道不太一樣，但我們還是很喜歡。

passages.title: 日本換新鈔了
passages.text: On July 3, 2024, Japan started using new banknotes for the first time in 20 years. The 10,000-yen bill shows Eiichi Shibusawa, a businessman who helped start hundreds of companies and Japan's first modern {1}. The 5,000-yen bill shows Umeko Tsuda, who started a school for women in 1900. The 1,000-yen bill shows Shibasaburo Kitasato, a scientist who fought diseases. The new bills have 3D holograms that make them very hard to copy. On the first day, many people lined up at {2} to get the new bills. Shops, {3}, and train stations had to update their ticket and vending machines. When my family visited Tokyo last winter, a small {4} gave me a new 1,000-yen bill as change. I didn't want to spend it! I kept it inside a guidebook I had bought at a {5} in Taipei.

blanks.why: Japan's first modern bank「日本第一家現代銀行」。spoon（湯匙）、cough（咳嗽）、fever（發燒）都不能由企業家「創立」。
lined up at banks to get the new bills「在銀行排隊換新鈔」。socks（襪子）、lemons（檸檬）、towels（毛巾）都不能換鈔票。
Shops, restaurants, and train stations「商店、餐廳和車站」，都有販賣機或售票機。soups（湯）、blankets（毯子）、candles（蠟燭）都不是場所。
a small bakery gave me a bill as change「一家小麵包店找錢給我一張鈔票」。sugar（糖）、noise（噪音）、weather（天氣）都不能找錢。
bought at a bookstore「在書店買的」旅遊書。pumpkin（南瓜）、fever、sock 都不賣書。

passages.zh: 2024 年 7 月 3 日，日本開始發行 20 年來第一次的新鈔。一萬日圓鈔票上是澀澤榮一，他是一位企業家，協助創立了好幾百家公司，以及日本第一家現代銀行。五千日圓上是津田梅子，她在 1900 年創辦了一所女子學校。一千日圓上是北里柴三郎，一位對抗疾病的科學家。新鈔有立體全像圖，非常難偽造。第一天，很多人到銀行排隊換新鈔。商店、餐廳和車站都得更新售票機和販賣機。我們家去年冬天去東京時，一家小麵包店找給我一張新的一千日圓鈔票。我捨不得花！我把它夾在一本在台北書店買的旅遊書裡。

passages.title: 電影院為什麼賣爆米花
passages.text: Why do movie {1} sell popcorn? It started in the 1930s in the United States. Times were hard, and popcorn was cheap, tasty, and easy to make. Owners soon found that they could earn more money from popcorn than from tickets! Popcorn is also fun science. Each kernel of corn has a tiny bit of water inside. When it gets hot, at around 180 degrees Celsius, the water turns into steam. The steam pushes harder and harder until the hard shell bursts, and the soft inside puffs out. Today, you can buy popcorn not only at the {2}, but also at night markets, {3}, and even some {4}. My little brother read about it in a science book from the {5}. Now, every time we watch a movie, he explains to everyone why the corn pops. My mom says she just wants to eat it in peace.

blanks.why: movie theaters sell popcorn「電影院賣爆米花」。spoons（湯匙）、coughs（咳嗽）、fevers（發燒）都不能和 movie 組成場所。
buy popcorn at the theater「在戲院買爆米花」。socks（襪子）、lemons（檸檬）、towels（毛巾）都不是買東西的地方。
night markets, restaurants「夜市、餐廳」，都是賣吃的地方。soups（湯）、blankets（毯子）、candles（蠟燭）都不是場所。
even some bakeries「甚至一些麵包店」。sugars（糖）、noises（噪音）、weathers（天氣）都不是店。
a science book from the bookstore「從書店買的科學書」。pumpkin（南瓜）、fever、sock 都不賣書。

passages.zh: 電影院為什麼賣爆米花？這要從 1930 年代的美國說起。當時日子很難過，而爆米花便宜、好吃又容易做。老闆們很快就發現，賣爆米花賺的錢比賣票還多！爆米花也藏著有趣的科學。每顆玉米粒裡都有一點點水分，加熱到大約攝氏 180 度時，水會變成蒸氣，蒸氣越推越用力，直到堅硬的外殼爆開，裡面柔軟的部分就膨脹出來。今天，你不只能在戲院買到爆米花，夜市、餐廳，甚至一些麵包店也買得到。我弟弟在一本從書店買的科學書上讀到這些。現在每次我們看電影，他都要跟大家解釋玉米為什麼會爆開。媽媽說她只想安安靜靜地吃。

passages.title: 切洋蔥為什麼會流眼淚
passages.text: Cooks in every {1} know this problem: cutting onions makes you cry. Why? When you cut an onion, you break its cells. This releases chemicals that mix together and make a gas. When the gas reaches your eyes, it bothers them, and your eyes make tears to wash it away. It's the onion's way of protecting itself from animals that want to eat it. There are some tricks to help. Putting the onion in the refrigerator for a while before cutting it slows down the gas. A sharp knife also breaks fewer cells, so less gas comes out. My uncle is a chef at a Japanese {2}, and he cuts about 50 onions every morning. He says he hardly cries anymore. My aunt runs a {3} next door, and she makes onion bread with his onions. Last week, I read about this in a cooking book from the {4}. Then I tried it at home. I still cried, but my mom said I looked like an actor in a sad movie at the {5}.

blanks.why: cooks in every restaurant「每家餐廳的廚師」。spoon（湯匙）、cough（咳嗽）、fever（發燒）都不是工作場所。
a chef at a Japanese restaurant「日本料理餐廳的主廚」。sock（襪子）、lemon（檸檬）、towel（毛巾）都不能雇用廚師。
runs a bakery「經營一家麵包店」，做洋蔥麵包。soup（湯）、blanket（毯子）、candle（蠟燭）都不能經營。
a cooking book from the bookstore「從書店買的烹飪書」。sugar（糖）、noise（噪音）、weather（天氣）都不賣書。
a sad movie at the theater「戲院裡的悲傷電影」。pumpkin（南瓜）、fever、sock 都不放電影。

passages.zh: 每家餐廳的廚師都知道這個問題：切洋蔥會讓人流眼淚。為什麼呢？切洋蔥時會破壞它的細胞，釋放出一些化學物質，它們混合後會產生一種氣體。氣體飄到眼睛時會刺激眼睛，眼睛就會流淚把它沖掉。這是洋蔥保護自己、不被動物吃掉的方法。有一些小技巧能幫忙：切之前先把洋蔥放進冰箱冰一陣子，可以讓氣體產生得比較慢；用鋒利的刀子也會破壞比較少的細胞，跑出來的氣體就比較少。我舅舅是一家日本料理餐廳的主廚，每天早上要切大約 50 顆洋蔥，他說他現在幾乎不會哭了。我阿姨在隔壁開麵包店，用他的洋蔥做洋蔥麵包。上週，我在從書店買的烹飪書裡讀到這些，回家試了一下。我還是哭了，但媽媽說我看起來像戲院悲傷電影裡的演員。

passages.title: 舊書為什麼有香草味
passages.text: Have you ever walked into an old {1} and noticed a sweet smell? Scientists say that this smell comes from the paper slowly breaking down. Paper is made from wood, and wood has a material called lignin. As old paper gets older, lignin breaks down into chemicals that smell a little like vanilla. Other chemicals smell a bit like grass or almonds. That's why old books often smell sweet and a little dusty. Some scientists even study the smell to learn how old a book is and how to protect it. New books smell different because of the ink and glue. My grandpa owns a used {2} near a temple. Next to it is a {3}, so his shop always smells like old books and fresh bread. He says customers come for both smells. On weekends, he also sells old movie posters from a closed {4}. He keeps all the money in a little box instead of the {5}, because he likes counting it every night.

blanks.why: walked into an old bookstore「走進一家舊書店」，文章在講舊書的味道。spoon（湯匙）、cough（咳嗽）、fever（發燒）都不能走進去。
owns a used bookstore「開了一間二手書店」。sock（襪子）、lemon（檸檬）、towel（毛巾）都不能經營。
Next to it is a bakery「隔壁是一家麵包店」，所以有新鮮麵包香。soup（湯）、blanket（毯子）、candle（蠟燭）都不是店。
posters from a closed theater「一家關門的戲院留下的海報」。sugar（糖）、noise（噪音）、weather（天氣）都沒有電影海報。
instead of the bank「而不是銀行」，指存錢的地方。pumpkin（南瓜）、fever、sock 都不能存錢。

passages.zh: 你有沒有走進舊書店時，聞到一股甜甜的味道？科學家說，這種味道來自紙張慢慢分解。紙是用木頭做的，木頭裡有一種叫做木質素的物質。紙越來越舊時，木質素會分解成聞起來有點像香草的化學物質，其他物質則有點像青草或杏仁的味道，所以舊書常常聞起來甜甜的，還帶點灰塵味。有些科學家甚至研究這種味道，用來判斷書有多老、該怎麼保護它。新書的味道不一樣，是因為墨水和膠水。我爺爺在一間廟旁邊開二手書店，隔壁是一家麵包店，所以他的店總是飄著舊書和新鮮麵包的香味。他說客人是為了這兩種味道而來的。週末時，他也賣一家已關門的戲院留下來的老電影海報。他把所有的錢放在一個小盒子裡，而不是存在銀行，因為他喜歡每天晚上數錢。

passages.title: 撲滿為什麼是小豬
passages.text: Why do many children keep coins in a "piggy {1}"? One popular explanation goes back hundreds of years to Europe. People stored money in pots made of a cheap orange clay called "pygg." Over time, the word "pygg" sounded like "pig," and potters began making money pots in the shape of pigs. Whether or not this story is completely true, the pig became a symbol of saving money around the world. Today, most people keep their savings in real {2}, but many families still give children piggy banks to teach them to save. When I was six, my grandma gave me a pink one. I saved coins for a whole year. Then I broke it open and used the money to buy a storybook at the {3} and a strawberry cake at the {4}. I also treated my grandma to a bowl of noodles at a small {5}. She said it was the best meal she had ever had.

blanks.why: a piggy bank「小豬撲滿」，固定說法。spoon（湯匙）、cough（咳嗽）、fever（發燒）都不能和 piggy 組成存錢筒。
keep their savings in real banks「把存款放在真正的銀行」。socks（襪子）、lemons（檸檬）、towels（毛巾）都不是存錢的機構。
buy a storybook at the bookstore「在書店買故事書」。soup（湯）、blanket（毯子）、candle（蠟燭）都不賣書。
a strawberry cake at the bakery「在麵包店買草莓蛋糕」。sugar（糖）、noise（噪音）、weather（天氣）都不是店。
a bowl of noodles at a small restaurant「在小餐館吃一碗麵」。pumpkin（南瓜）、fever、sock 都不是吃飯的地方。

passages.zh: 為什麼很多小孩會把硬幣存在「小豬撲滿」裡？有一個很流行的說法要回到幾百年前的歐洲：當時人們把錢存在一種用便宜的橘色黏土做成的罐子裡，這種黏土叫做「pygg」。久而久之，「pygg」聽起來像「pig（豬）」，陶工就開始做成小豬形狀的存錢罐。不管這個故事是不是完全正確，小豬已經成為全世界存錢的象徵。今天，大部分人把存款放在真正的銀行裡，但很多家庭還是會送小孩小豬撲滿，教他們存錢。我六歲時，奶奶送我一個粉紅色的撲滿。我存了一整年的硬幣，然後把它打破，用那些錢在書店買了一本故事書，在麵包店買了一個草莓蛋糕，還請奶奶在一家小餐館吃了一碗麵。她說那是她吃過最棒的一餐。

passages.title: 幸運餅乾其實來自日本
passages.text: If you eat at a Chinese {1} in the United States, you will often get a fortune cookie at the end of the meal. Inside the crunchy cookie is a small paper with a message, like "Good luck is coming your way." Many people think fortune cookies come from China, but that's a myth. You can hardly find them in China! Researchers believe they started in Japan, where a {2} in Kyoto made a similar cookie with a fortune inside. In the early 1900s, Japanese immigrants in California began selling them. Later, Chinese {3} in America began serving them, and they became a symbol of Chinese American food. Last year, my family visited San Francisco. We saw a small factory where workers folded the cookies by hand. I bought a bag and a book about their history at a {4} in Chinatown. My fortune said, "You will find money soon." The next day, I found 20 dollars near a {5} and gave it to the police!

blanks.why: eat at a Chinese restaurant「在中餐廳吃飯」。spoon（湯匙）、cough（咳嗽）、fever（發燒）都不是吃飯的場所。
a bakery in Kyoto made a similar cookie「京都一家糕餅店做出類似的餅乾」。sock（襪子）、lemon（檸檬）、towel（毛巾）都不會做餅乾。
Chinese restaurants began serving them「中餐廳開始提供這種餅乾」。soups（湯）、blankets（毯子）、candles（蠟燭）都不能供應食物給客人。
a book at a bookstore in Chinatown「在中國城書店買的書」。sugar（糖）、noise（噪音）、weather（天氣）都不賣書。
found 20 dollars near a bank「在銀行附近撿到 20 元」。pumpkin（南瓜）、fever、sock 都不是地點。

passages.zh: 如果你在美國的中餐廳吃飯，飯後常會拿到一個幸運餅乾。酥脆的餅乾裡夾著一張小紙條，上面寫著像「好運即將到來」這樣的話。很多人以為幸運餅乾來自中國，但這是迷思——在中國幾乎找不到！研究人員認為它起源於日本，京都一家糕餅店曾做出一種夾著籤詩的類似餅乾。1900 年代初，加州的日本移民開始販賣這種餅乾。後來美國的中餐廳開始提供它，它就成了美式中華料理的象徵。去年我們家去舊金山，看到一間小工廠裡工人用手摺餅乾。我在中國城的書店買了一包餅乾和一本講它歷史的書。我的籤詩寫著：「你很快會找到錢。」隔天，我在一家銀行附近撿到 20 元，交給了警察！

passages.title: 兩千多年前的超強音響
passages.text: More than 2,300 years ago, the ancient Greeks built a huge open-air {1} at Epidaurus. It has about 14,000 stone seats in a half circle on a hillside. It is famous for its amazing sound. Visitors say that a person standing in the center can speak softly, and people in the top row can still hear. In 2007, scientists found one reason: the rows of stone seats block low sounds like wind and crowd noise but let the higher sounds of voices travel up the hill. Many modern {2} still learn from its design, and plays are still performed there in summer. Last summer, my aunt visited Greece. She stood at the center and sang a Taiwanese song, and her husband heard her clearly from the top. After the visit, they ate at a seaside {3} and bought sweet bread from a village {4}. She also bought me a book about Greek myths at a {5} in Athens.

blanks.why: a huge open-air theater「一座巨大的露天劇場」。spoon（湯匙）、cough（咳嗽）、fever（發燒）都不能有一萬四千個座位。
Many modern theaters still learn from its design「很多現代劇院仍學習它的設計」。socks（襪子）、lemons（檸檬）、towels（毛巾）都不需要考慮音響。
ate at a seaside restaurant「在海邊的餐廳吃飯」。soup（湯）、blanket（毯子）、candle（蠟燭）都不是吃飯的地方。
sweet bread from a village bakery「村裡麵包店的甜麵包」。sugar（糖）、noise（噪音）、weather（天氣）都不是店。
bought a book at a bookstore「在書店買書」。pumpkin（南瓜）、fever、sock 都不賣書。

passages.zh: 兩千三百多年前，古希臘人在埃皮達魯斯蓋了一座巨大的露天劇場。它在山坡上有大約一萬四千個半圓形排列的石頭座位，以神奇的音響效果聞名。遊客說，站在中央的人輕聲說話，坐在最上排的人仍然聽得到。2007 年，科學家找到了一個原因：一排排的石頭座位會擋住風聲和人群吵雜聲這類低沉的聲音，卻讓人聲這種較高的聲音傳上山坡。很多現代劇院仍向它的設計學習，夏天時那裡還會上演戲劇。去年夏天我阿姨去了希臘，她站在中央唱了一首台灣歌，她先生在最上排聽得清清楚楚。參觀完後，他們在海邊的餐廳吃飯，還在村子裡的麵包店買了甜麵包。她也在雅典的書店買了一本希臘神話的書送我。

passages.title: 「夢劇場」老特拉福
passages.text: Old Trafford, the home of Manchester United in England, has a famous nickname: the "Theatre of Dreams." The name was given by Bobby Charlton, one of the club's greatest players. It is one of the biggest soccer stadiums in England, with room for about 74,000 fans. For many fans, watching a match there feels like watching a great show in a {1}. On match days, the streets nearby are full of people. Every {2} and pub is crowded, and a small {3} near the stadium sells pies to hungry fans. The stadium also has a museum and a shop that sells books about the club's history. My cousin studies in Manchester. Before his first match, he took money out of the {4} to buy a ticket and a red scarf. He also bought a book about the team at a {5} in the city center. He says that when 74,000 people sing together, it really feels like a dream.

blanks.why: a great show in a theater「劇院裡的精彩表演」，比喻看球像看戲。spoon（湯匙）、cough（咳嗽）、fever（發燒）都不能上演表演。
Every restaurant and pub is crowded「每家餐廳和酒吧都擠滿人」。sock（襪子）、lemon（檸檬）、towel（毛巾）都不會擠滿人。
a small bakery sells pies「一家小麵包店賣派」。soup（湯）、blanket（毯子）、candle（蠟燭）都不能賣東西。
took money out of the bank「從銀行領錢」。sugar（糖）、noise（噪音）、weather（天氣）都不能領錢。
bought a book at a bookstore「在書店買書」。pumpkin（南瓜）、fever、sock 都不賣書。

passages.zh: 英格蘭曼聯的主場老特拉福有一個有名的綽號：「夢劇場」。這個名字是曼聯史上最偉大的球員之一巴比‧查爾頓取的。它是英格蘭最大的足球場之一，可以容納大約七萬四千名球迷。對很多球迷來說，在那裡看球就像在劇院看一場精彩的表演。比賽日時，附近的街道擠滿了人，每家餐廳和酒吧都客滿，球場附近一家小麵包店會賣派給肚子餓的球迷。球場裡還有博物館和賣球隊歷史書的商店。我表哥在曼徹斯特念書。第一次看比賽前，他從銀行領錢買了一張票和一條紅色圍巾，還在市中心的書店買了一本講球隊的書。他說，當七萬四千人一起唱歌時，真的像在做夢一樣。

passages.title: 鄧肯的擦板球
passages.text: In basketball, a "{1} shot" is a shot that hits the backboard first and then goes into the basket. Many players think it's old-fashioned, but Tim Duncan made it famous. Duncan played 19 seasons for the San Antonio Spurs and won five championships. He was so calm and careful that people called him "The Big Fundamental." His favorite move was a simple bank shot from the side, and he made it again and again. Some young players today practice it because it is hard to block. My PE teacher loves Duncan. Last week, he showed us how to use the corner of the square on the backboard. I tried 20 times and made 12! After practice, our team went to a noodle {2} to celebrate. On the way home, I stopped at a {3} for a melon bun and then at a {4} to look for a book about Duncan. They didn't have one, so I watched his old games online instead. Later that night, I joked to my dad that I wanted to put all my basketballs in the {5} because they're so valuable now.

blanks.why: a bank shot「擦板球」，籃球術語，bank 在這裡指打板。spoon（湯匙）、cough（咳嗽）、fever（發燒）都不能和 shot 組成籃球用語。
went to a noodle restaurant「去一家麵店」。sock（襪子）、lemon（檸檬）、towel（毛巾）都不能和 noodle 組成用餐地點。
stopped at a bakery for a melon bun「在麵包店停下來買菠蘿麵包」。soup（湯）、blanket（毯子）、candle（蠟燭）都不是店。
a bookstore to look for a book「去書店找書」。sugar（糖）、noise（噪音）、weather（天氣）都不賣書。
put my basketballs in the bank「把籃球存進銀行」，開玩笑說它們很珍貴。pumpkin（南瓜）、fever、sock 都不是存放貴重物品的地方。

passages.zh: 在籃球裡，「擦板球」是指球先打到籃板再進籃框的投籃。很多球員覺得它很老派，但提姆‧鄧肯讓它變得很有名。鄧肯在聖安東尼奧馬刺隊打了 19 個球季，拿下五座總冠軍。他冷靜又細心，大家叫他「大基本功」。他最喜歡的招式就是從側邊投一記簡單的擦板球，而且一投再投。現在有些年輕球員也練這招，因為它很難被封阻。我的體育老師很愛鄧肯。上週他教我們瞄準籃板上方框的角落，我投了 20 次進了 12 次！練完球後，我們球隊去一家麵店慶祝。回家路上，我先到麵包店買了一個菠蘿麵包，又去書店找講鄧肯的書。書店沒有，所以我改上網看他以前的比賽。那天晚上，我跟爸爸開玩笑說，我想把所有籃球存進銀行，因為它們現在太珍貴了。

passages.title: 菲爾普斯一天吃一萬兩千大卡？
passages.text: At the 2008 Beijing Olympics, American swimmer Michael Phelps won eight gold medals, a record for one Olympics. Around that time, newspapers reported that he ate about 12,000 calories a day. Stories said that his breakfast alone included egg sandwiches, pancakes, and French toast. Later, Phelps said that number was too high, but it was true that he needed a lot of food, because he swam for hours every day. Many athletes eat huge meals while training. Some {1} near training centers even make special big plates for swimmers. My cousin is on her school swim team. After practice, she always stops at a {2} and buys three pieces of bread. On weekends, our family takes her to a buffet {3}, and she eats more than my dad! She also read a book about Phelps that she bought at a {4}. Her dream is to swim at the Olympics. "And to have enough money in the {5} to pay for all my food," she laughs.

blanks.why: Some restaurants make special big plates「有些餐廳做特大份的餐點」。spoons（湯匙）、coughs（咳嗽）、fevers（發燒）都不能做餐點。
stops at a bakery and buys bread「在麵包店停下來買麵包」。socks（襪子）、lemons（檸檬）、towels（毛巾）都不是店。
a buffet restaurant「吃到飽餐廳」。soup（湯）、blanket（毯子）、candle（蠟燭）都不能和 buffet 組成用餐地點。
bought at a bookstore「在書店買的」書。sugar（糖）、noise（噪音）、weather（天氣）都不賣書。
enough money in the bank「銀行裡有足夠的錢」。pumpkin（南瓜）、fever、sock 都不能存錢。

passages.zh: 在 2008 年北京奧運，美國游泳選手麥可‧菲爾普斯拿下八面金牌，創下單屆奧運的紀錄。那時候報紙報導他一天大約吃一萬兩千大卡，故事說光是他的早餐就有蛋三明治、鬆餅和法式吐司。後來菲爾普斯說那個數字太誇張了，但他確實需要吃很多，因為他每天要游好幾個小時。很多運動員在訓練期間都吃得很多，有些訓練中心附近的餐廳甚至為游泳選手做特大份的餐點。我表姊是學校游泳隊的隊員，練完游泳總會到麵包店買三個麵包。週末時，我們全家帶她去吃到飽餐廳，她吃得比我爸還多！她也讀了一本在書店買的菲爾普斯傳記。她的夢想是到奧運游泳。她笑著說：「還有，銀行裡要有足夠的錢付我所有的伙食費。」

passages.title: 柯比的《曼巴精神》
passages.text: In 2018, Kobe Bryant, one of the greatest basketball players of all time, published a book called The Mamba Mentality: How I Play. In it, he explained how he studied the game, trained his body, and never stopped trying to get better. The book became a bestseller, and it is still popular today in {1} around the world. Bryant played 20 seasons for the Los Angeles Lakers and won five championships. He was famous for practicing early in the morning, before other players woke up. My older brother is a big fan. He saved his money in the {2} for months to buy a special copy of the book. He bought it at a big {3} in Taipei and read it at a café inside. He even started getting up at five to practice, just like Kobe. After practice, he buys breakfast at a {4} near the court. Last month, his team won the school championship, and they celebrated at a hot pot {5}.

blanks.why: popular in bookstores「在書店很受歡迎」。spoons（湯匙）、coughs（咳嗽）、fevers（發燒）都不賣書。
saved his money in the bank「把錢存在銀行」。socks（襪子）、lemons（檸檬）、towels（毛巾）都不能存錢。
bought it at a big bookstore「在一家大書店買的」，裡面還有咖啡廳。soup（湯）、blanket（毯子）、candle（蠟燭）都不是店。
buys breakfast at a bakery「在麵包店買早餐」。sugar（糖）、noise（噪音）、weather（天氣）都不賣早餐。
celebrated at a hot pot restaurant「在火鍋餐廳慶祝」。pumpkin（南瓜）、fever、sock 都不能和 hot pot 組成用餐地點。

passages.zh: 2018 年，史上最偉大的籃球員之一柯比‧布萊恩出版了一本書，叫做《曼巴精神：柯比‧布萊恩自述》。他在書裡說明自己怎麼研究比賽、鍛鍊身體，以及如何不停努力變得更好。這本書成了暢銷書，到現在在世界各地的書店仍然很受歡迎。柯比在洛杉磯湖人隊打了 20 個球季，拿下五座總冠軍，他以比其他球員更早起床、一大早就練球而聞名。我哥哥是他的超級粉絲，在銀行存了好幾個月的錢，才買到一本特別版。他在台北一家大書店買下它，就在店裡的咖啡廳讀。他甚至開始像柯比一樣五點起床練球，練完後在球場附近的麵包店買早餐。上個月他的球隊拿下校內冠軍，大家去一家火鍋餐廳慶祝。

passages.title: 全世界最大的餐廳在奧運村
passages.text: During the Paris 2024 Olympics, the athletes' village had what some reporters called the biggest {1} in the world. It had about 3,500 seats and served up to 40,000 meals a day to athletes from more than 200 countries. The cooks made food from many cultures, and more than half of the dishes had no meat. There was even a French {2} corner with fresh bread and croissants every morning. One food became famous online: the chocolate muffins. A Norwegian swimmer, Henrik Christiansen, posted many videos about how much he loved them, and millions of people watched. Some fans called him "the Muffin Man." Soon after, my aunt, who owns a small {3} in Kaohsiung, started selling "Olympic muffins," and they sold out every day! My sister, who is a swimmer, watched all his videos. She went to a {4} and bought a baking book so she could make the muffins at home. They were delicious, and she said she would save money in the {5} to go to the Olympics one day.

blanks.why: the biggest restaurant in the world「世界最大的餐廳」，有 3,500 個座位。spoon（湯匙）、cough（咳嗽）、fever（發燒）都不能供應餐點。
a French bakery corner「一個法式麵包區」，有麵包和可頌。sock（襪子）、lemon（檸檬）、towel（毛巾）都不能和 corner 組成賣麵包的地方。
owns a small bakery「開了一家小麵包店」，所以能賣馬芬。soup（湯）、blanket（毯子）、candle（蠟燭）都不能經營來賣點心。
went to a bookstore and bought a baking book「去書店買烘焙書」。sugar（糖）、noise（噪音）、weather（天氣）都不賣書。
save money in the bank「把錢存在銀行」。pumpkin（南瓜）、fever、sock 都不能存錢。

passages.zh: 在 2024 年巴黎奧運期間，選手村裡有一間被記者稱為「全世界最大的餐廳」。它有大約 3,500 個座位，每天最多供應四萬份餐點給來自兩百多個國家的選手。廚師做出許多不同文化的料理，超過一半的菜沒有肉。那裡甚至有一個法式麵包區，每天早上都有新鮮的麵包和可頌。其中一樣食物在網路上爆紅：巧克力馬芬。挪威游泳選手亨里克‧克里斯蒂安森上傳了很多影片，說他有多愛這種馬芬，吸引好幾百萬人觀看，有些粉絲叫他「馬芬人」。不久後，我在高雄開小麵包店的阿姨也開始賣「奧運馬芬」，每天都賣光！我的游泳選手姊姊看了他所有的影片，還去書店買了一本烘焙書，好在家裡自己做馬芬。做出來的馬芬很好吃，她說她要在銀行存錢，有一天也要去奧運。

passages.title: 詹皇蓋的學校
passages.text: In 2018, NBA star LeBron James helped open the I Promise School in his hometown of Akron, Ohio. It is a public school for children who need extra help with reading and math. Many of the students come from families that don't have much money. The school gives students free uniforms, bikes, and healthy food. There is even a food {1} where families can get groceries for free, so children don't come to school hungry. LeBron said he wanted to give kids the chances he didn't have when he was young. Local {2} and a {3} near the school also give food to the families. A {4} in the city gave books for the school library. My PE teacher showed us a video about the school. After class, our class decided to collect canned food for a food bank in our city. We brought cans from home and gave them to a {5} owner who drives the food there every week. It felt good to help, just like LeBron.

blanks.why: a food bank「食物銀行」，免費提供食物給需要的人。spoon（湯匙）、cough（咳嗽）、fever（發燒）都不能和 food 組成這種機構。
Local restaurants give food「當地餐廳捐食物」。socks（襪子）、lemons（檸檬）、towels（毛巾）都不能捐食物。
a bakery near the school「學校附近的麵包店」。soup（湯）、blanket（毯子）、candle（蠟燭）都不是店。
A bookstore gave books「一家書店捐書」。sugar（糖）、noise（噪音）、weather（天氣）都不能捐書。
gave them to a restaurant owner「交給一位餐廳老闆」，他每週把食物載過去。pumpkin（南瓜）、fever、sock 都不能和 owner 組成「開店的人」。

passages.zh: 2018 年，NBA 球星勒布朗‧詹姆斯在他的家鄉俄亥俄州阿克倫協助成立了「我承諾學校」。這是一所公立學校，招收需要在閱讀和數學上額外協助的孩子，很多學生的家庭經濟並不寬裕。學校提供學生免費的制服、腳踏車和健康的食物，甚至還有一個「食物銀行」，讓家庭可以免費領取食物，孩子就不會餓著肚子上學。勒布朗說，他想給孩子們他小時候沒有的機會。當地的餐廳和學校附近的一家麵包店也捐食物給這些家庭，市區一家書店則捐書給學校圖書館。體育老師給我們看了這所學校的影片。下課後，我們班決定替市內的食物銀行收集罐頭。我們從家裡帶罐頭來，交給一位每週開車把食物送過去的餐廳老闆。能幫助別人的感覺很好，就像勒布朗一樣。

passages.title: 台灣第一間同志書店
passages.text: In 1999, a small {1} called Gin Gin's opened in Taipei. It was the first bookstore in Taiwan made especially for LGBT+ readers. At that time, it was hard to find books about gay, lesbian, or transgender people in normal {2}. Gin Gin's gave people a safe place to read, meet friends, and feel accepted. Over the years, it has also sold rainbow flags, cards, and books for families who want to learn more. Many visitors from other countries come to see it, and some say it helped them feel less alone. Last month, my class visited the area on a field trip about human rights. Our teacher said that everyone deserves to see their own stories in books. After the visit, we ate lunch at a {3} nearby, and the owner gave us free cookies from the {4} next door. Then our teacher took us to a {5} to watch a short film about a teenager who learns to be proud of who she is.

blanks.why: a small bookstore opened「一家小書店開幕」，後面說它是同志書店。spoon（湯匙）、cough（咳嗽）、fever（發燒）都不能「開幕」賣書。
in normal bookstores「在一般書店」。socks（襪子）、lemons（檸檬）、towels（毛巾）都不是找書的地方。
ate lunch at a restaurant「在餐廳吃午餐」。soup（湯）、blanket（毯子）、candle（蠟燭）都不是用餐場所。
cookies from the bakery next door「隔壁麵包店的餅乾」。sugar（糖）、noise（噪音）、weather（天氣）都不是店。
took us to a theater to watch a film「帶我們去戲院看片」。pumpkin（南瓜）、fever、sock 都不能放電影。

passages.zh: 1999 年，一家叫做「晶晶書庫」的小書店在台北開幕，它是台灣第一家專為多元性別讀者開設的書店。在那個年代，一般書店很難找到關於同志或跨性別者的書。晶晶書庫給了大家一個可以安心看書、認識朋友、感覺被接納的地方。這些年來，它也販賣彩虹旗、卡片，以及給想多了解的家庭看的書。很多外國遊客也會來參觀，有人說這裡讓他們不再那麼孤單。上個月，我們班參加人權主題的校外教學，到那一帶參觀。老師說，每個人都值得在書裡看到屬於自己的故事。參觀完後，我們在附近的餐廳吃午餐，老闆還送我們隔壁麵包店的餅乾。接著老師帶我們去戲院看一部短片，講一個青少女學會為自己感到驕傲的故事。

passages.title: 女性也能自己辦信用卡
passages.text: Not so long ago, many women in the United States could not easily get a credit card or a loan by themselves. Some {1} asked a woman to bring her husband or father to sign the papers, even if she had her own job and money. On October 28, 1974, a law called the Equal Credit Opportunity Act changed this. It said that a {2} could not treat people differently because of whether they were men or women, or because they were married or single. After that, women could open their own businesses more easily, such as a small {3}, a {4}, or a family {5}. In 2024, the Smithsonian museum in Washington marked the law's 50th birthday. When my grandma heard this story, she said that when she opened her noodle shop in Taiwan, she also needed her brother to help her borrow money. "Now your mom can do it alone," she said proudly.

blanks.why: Some banks asked a woman to bring her husband「有些銀行要求女性帶丈夫來」。spoons（湯匙）、coughs（咳嗽）、fevers（發燒）都不能要求別人簽文件。
a bank could not treat people differently「銀行不能差別對待」。sock（襪子）、lemon（檸檬）、towel（毛巾）都不會辦貸款。
a small bakery「一家小麵包店」，是女性可以開的店。soup（湯）、blanket（毯子）、candle（蠟燭）都不能「經營」成生意。
a bookstore「一家書店」。sugar（糖）、noise（噪音）、weather（天氣）都不是店。
a family restaurant「一家家庭餐廳」。pumpkin（南瓜）、fever、sock 都不能和 family 組成店家。

passages.zh: 不久以前，美國很多女性還很難自己辦信用卡或申請貸款。即使她們有自己的工作和收入，有些銀行還是要求女性帶丈夫或父親來簽文件。1974 年 10 月 28 日，《平等信用機會法》改變了這個情況。它規定銀行不能因為一個人是男是女、已婚或單身而有不同的待遇。從那之後，女性更容易自己創業，例如開一家小麵包店、一家書店，或一家家庭餐廳。2024 年，華盛頓的史密森尼博物館紀念這項法律通過 50 週年。奶奶聽到這個故事時說，她當年在台灣開麵店時，也需要哥哥幫忙才借得到錢。她驕傲地說：「現在妳媽媽一個人就辦得到了。」

passages.title: 會上錯菜的餐廳
passages.text: In 2017, a TV director in Tokyo named Shiro Oguni opened a special pop-up {1} called "The Restaurant of Mistaken Orders." All the servers were older people living with dementia, a disease that makes it hard to remember things. Sometimes they brought the wrong dishes or forgot who ordered what. But nobody complained. Customers smiled, laughed, and enjoyed talking with the servers. The idea was to help people understand dementia and to show that people with it can still work and enjoy life. The event became famous around the world, and other {2} in Japan and other countries later held similar events. My grandpa has dementia, too. Last month, our family took him to a small {3} where he used to buy bread. The owner remembered him and let him help put the buns on the shelf. Later, we watched an old movie at a small {4}, and he sang every song. On the way home, he stopped at a {5} and bought me a book. It was the wrong book, but it was the best gift.

blanks.why: a special pop-up restaurant「一家特別的快閃餐廳」。spoon（湯匙）、cough（咳嗽）、fever（發燒）都不能有服務生。
other restaurants held similar events「其他餐廳也舉辦類似活動」。socks（襪子）、lemons（檸檬）、towels（毛巾）都不能辦活動。
a small bakery where he used to buy bread「他以前常去買麵包的小麵包店」。soup（湯）、blanket（毯子）、candle（蠟燭）都不是店。
watched an old movie at a small theater「在小戲院看老電影」。sugar（糖）、noise（噪音）、weather（天氣）都不能放電影。
stopped at a bookstore and bought me a book「在書店停下來買書給我」。pumpkin（南瓜）、fever、sock 都不賣書。

passages.zh: 2017 年，東京一位名叫小國士朗的電視導演開了一家特別的快閃餐廳，叫做「會上錯菜的餐廳」。所有的服務生都是罹患失智症的長者，這種病會讓人很難記住事情。有時候他們會上錯菜，或忘記誰點了什麼，但沒有人抱怨。客人們笑著和服務生聊天，玩得很開心。這個點子是要幫助大家了解失智症，也讓人看到失智的人仍然可以工作、享受生活。這個活動傳遍全世界，後來日本和其他國家的餐廳也舉辦了類似的活動。我爺爺也有失智症。上個月，我們全家帶他去以前常去買麵包的小麵包店。老闆還記得他，讓他幫忙把麵包擺上架。之後，我們在一間小戲院看老電影，他每首歌都跟著唱。回家路上，他在一家書店停下來，買了一本書給我。雖然那是一本錯的書，卻是最棒的禮物。

passages.title: 用手語點咖啡
passages.text: In October 2018, Starbucks opened its first U.S. "signing store" in Washington, D.C., near Gallaudet University, a university for deaf students. All the workers there know American Sign Language, and many of them are deaf or hard of hearing. Customers can order by signing, writing, or using a tablet. The store's design helps, too: it has bright lights and open spaces so people can see each other's hands easily. Since then, more cafés and {1} around the world have hired deaf workers. In Taiwan, too, some shops and a few {2} now have staff who use Taiwan Sign Language. My classmate Amy's parents are deaf. Last weekend, she took me to a sign language café near a {3} in Taipei. She taught me how to sign "thank you" and "delicious." After that, we went to a {4} to watch a movie with subtitles, and later we stopped at a {5} so she could help her mom with some papers. Now I want to learn more sign language.

blanks.why: more cafés and restaurants have hired deaf workers「更多咖啡廳和餐廳僱用聽障員工」。spoons（湯匙）、coughs（咳嗽）、fevers（發燒）都不能僱用人。
a few bakeries have staff「有些麵包店有員工」。socks（襪子）、lemons（檸檬）、towels（毛巾）都不是店。
a café near a bookstore「一家書店附近的咖啡廳」。soup（湯）、blanket（毯子）、candle（蠟燭）都不是地點。
went to a theater to watch a movie「去戲院看電影」。sugar（糖）、noise（噪音）、weather（天氣）都不能放電影。
stopped at a bank「去銀行一趟」，幫媽媽處理文件。pumpkin（南瓜）、fever、sock 都不是辦文件的地方。

passages.zh: 2018 年 10 月，星巴克在美國華盛頓特區開了第一家「手語門市」，就在聽障大學高立德大學附近。店裡所有員工都會美國手語，很多人本身就是聽障或重聽者。客人可以用手語、寫字或平板電腦點餐。店的設計也有幫助：燈光明亮、空間開闊，讓大家容易看清楚彼此的手。從那之後，世界各地有越來越多咖啡廳和餐廳僱用聽障員工。在台灣，也有一些商店和幾家麵包店有會台灣手語的員工。我同學艾美的爸媽是聽障者。上週末，她帶我去台北一家書店附近的手語咖啡廳，教我用手語比「謝謝」和「好吃」。之後我們去戲院看一部有字幕的電影，然後到銀行一趟，讓她幫媽媽處理一些文件。現在我很想多學一點手語。

passages.title: 在電影院大合唱的《K-POP 獵魔女團》
passages.text: In June 2025, Netflix released the animated movie KPop Demon Hunters. It tells the story of Huntr/x, a fictional K-pop girl group whose three members, Rumi, Mira, and Zoey, secretly fight demons with their songs. The movie became a huge hit around the world, and its song "Golden" reached number one on the Billboard Hot 100. In August 2025, Netflix held special sing-along shows in about 1,750 movie {1} in North America. Fans dressed up like the characters and sang every song. That weekend, it became the first Netflix movie to be number one at the North American box office. Some {2} and cafés near the shows even made "Golden" drinks and Korean snacks. In Taiwan, a {3} near my school sold cupcakes with the three members' faces on them. My friends and I bought six and ate them while we watched the movie at home. Later, I found a book about how the film was made at a {4}, but it was too expensive. I'm saving money in the {5} to buy it next month.

blanks.why: movie theaters「電影院」，舉辦合唱場。spoons（湯匙）、coughs（咳嗽）、fevers（發燒）都不能和 movie 組成場所。
restaurants and cafés made drinks「餐廳和咖啡廳推出飲料」。socks（襪子）、lemons（檸檬）、towels（毛巾）都不能做飲料賣。
a bakery sold cupcakes「一家麵包店賣杯子蛋糕」。soup（湯）、blanket（毯子）、candle（蠟燭）都不是店。
found a book at a bookstore「在書店找到一本書」。sugar（糖）、noise（噪音）、weather（天氣）都不賣書。
saving money in the bank「把錢存在銀行」。pumpkin（南瓜）、fever、sock 都不能存錢。

passages.zh: 2025 年 6 月，Netflix 推出動畫電影《K-POP 獵魔女團》。故事講的是虛構的 K-pop 女團 Huntr/x，三位成員 Rumi、Mira 和 Zoey 偷偷用歌聲對抗惡魔。這部電影在全世界大受歡迎，主題曲〈Golden〉還登上告示牌百大單曲榜第一名。2025 年 8 月，Netflix 在北美大約 1,750 家電影院舉辦特別的跟唱場。粉絲們打扮成角色，跟著唱每一首歌。那個週末，它成為第一部登上北美票房冠軍的 Netflix 電影。有些餐廳和咖啡廳甚至在附近推出「Golden」飲料和韓國小吃。在台灣，我學校附近的一家麵包店賣起印有三位成員臉的杯子蛋糕。我和朋友買了六個，邊在家看電影邊吃。後來我在書店找到一本講這部電影怎麼製作的書，可是太貴了。我正在銀行存錢，打算下個月買。

passages.title: 在電影院看 BTS 的釜山演唱會
passages.text: On February 1, 2023, BTS fans around the world went to movie {1} to watch BTS: Yet to Come in Cinemas. The film showed the group's free concert in Busan in October 2022, which was held to support the city's bid to host the World Expo. Because it was shown in {2} in many countries, fans who couldn't go to Busan could finally see the show on a big screen. Many fans brought light sticks and sang along as if they were at a real concert. In Taipei, some fans held small parties at a {3} before the movie, and a {4} near the theater sold purple cakes. My sister went with her friends from school. Before the show, she bought a BTS photo book at a {5} next to the cinema. When the members sang "Yet to Come," she cried, and so did the people sitting next to her. "It felt like we were all in Busan together," she told me.

blanks.why: went to movie theaters「去電影院」。spoons（湯匙）、coughs（咳嗽）、fevers（發燒）都不能和 movie 組成場所。
shown in theaters in many countries「在很多國家的戲院上映」。socks（襪子）、lemons（檸檬）、towels（毛巾）都不能放電影。
held small parties at a restaurant「在餐廳辦小派對」。soup（湯）、blanket（毯子）、candle（蠟燭）都不是辦派對的地方。
a bakery sold purple cakes「一家麵包店賣紫色蛋糕」。sugar（糖）、noise（噪音）、weather（天氣）都不是店。
bought a photo book at a bookstore「在書店買寫真書」。pumpkin（南瓜）、fever、sock 都不賣書。

passages.zh: 2023 年 2 月 1 日，世界各地的 BTS 粉絲走進電影院觀看《BTS: Yet to Come in Cinemas》。這部片記錄了 BTS 在 2022 年 10 月於釜山舉辦的免費演唱會，那場演唱會是為了支持釜山爭取主辦世界博覽會。因為在很多國家的戲院上映，無法去釜山的粉絲終於能在大螢幕上看到這場演出。很多粉絲帶著應援手燈，像在真正的演唱會一樣跟著唱。在台北，有些粉絲先在餐廳辦小派對再去看電影，戲院附近的一家麵包店還賣起紫色蛋糕。我姊姊和學校的朋友一起去看。開演前，她在電影院旁的書店買了一本 BTS 寫真書。成員們唱〈Yet to Come〉的時候，她哭了，坐在旁邊的人也哭了。她告訴我：「感覺就像我們全都一起在釜山。」

passages.title: 首爾的星空圖書館
passages.text: In COEX Mall in Gangnam, Seoul, there is a huge open library called Starfield Library. It opened in 2017, and its giant bookshelves are about 13 meters tall, filled with tens of thousands of books and magazines. Anyone can sit down and read for free. It has become one of the most popular photo spots in Seoul, especially for K-pop fans who visit Gangnam, because many entertainment companies are nearby. The mall around it has many {1}, cafés, a {2} that sells Korean sweet bread, a movie {3}, and even an aquarium. My cousin visited last summer. She said it looked like a {4} built for giants! She sat under the tall shelves and read a K-pop magazine for an hour. Then she watched a movie, ate cold noodles, and exchanged some money at a {5} in the mall. "I could spend a whole day there," she said.

blanks.why: many restaurants and cafés「很多餐廳和咖啡廳」。spoons（湯匙）、coughs（咳嗽）、fevers（發燒）都不是商場裡的店。
a bakery that sells sweet bread「一家賣甜麵包的麵包店」。socks（襪子）、lemons（檸檬）、towels（毛巾）都不賣麵包。
a movie theater「電影院」。soup（湯）、blanket（毯子）、candle（蠟燭）都不能和 movie 組成場所。
a bookstore built for giants「為巨人蓋的書店」，比喻書架非常高。sugar（糖）、noise（噪音）、weather（天氣）都沒有書架。
exchanged money at a bank「在銀行換錢」。pumpkin（南瓜）、fever、sock 都不能換錢。

passages.zh: 首爾江南的 COEX 商場裡，有一座巨大的開放式圖書館，叫做「星空圖書館」。它在 2017 年開幕，巨大的書架大約 13 公尺高，擺滿好幾萬本書和雜誌，任何人都可以免費坐下來閱讀。它成了首爾最受歡迎的拍照景點之一，特別是來江南的 K-pop 粉絲，因為很多經紀公司就在附近。周圍的商場裡有許多餐廳、咖啡廳、一家賣韓國甜麵包的麵包店、電影院，甚至還有水族館。我表姊去年夏天去過，她說那裡看起來像一家為巨人蓋的書店！她坐在高高的書架下看了一個小時的 K-pop 雜誌，接著看了一場電影、吃了冷麵，還在商場裡的銀行換了一些錢。她說：「我可以在那裡待一整天。」

passages.title: 偶像生日咖啡廳
passages.text: In Korea and many other places, K-pop fans have a special way to celebrate their favorite idol's birthday. They rent a café or a small {1} for a few days and decorate it with posters, photos, and balloons. These are called "birthday cafés." Fans who come can get free cup sleeves, stickers, and photo cards when they buy a drink. Some birthday cafés even work with a local {2} to sell cakes with the idol's face on them. In Taipei, too, fans hold birthday cafés for idols like Jungkook, Jimin, and Tzuyu, and the lines can go around the block. Last month, my friend Lily helped run one for Jungkook. She saved money in the {3} for half a year to pay for it. She printed the photo cards at a shop near a {4} and asked a nearby movie {5} to put up a poster, too. More than 300 fans came. "It was tiring," Lily said, "but seeing everyone smile made it worth it."

blanks.why: rent a café or a small restaurant「租一間咖啡廳或小餐廳」。spoon（湯匙）、cough（咳嗽）、fever（發燒）都不能租來辦活動。
work with a local bakery to sell cakes「和當地麵包店合作賣蛋糕」。sock（襪子）、lemon（檸檬）、towel（毛巾）都不會做蛋糕。
saved money in the bank「在銀行存錢」。soup（湯）、blanket（毯子）、candle（蠟燭）都不能存錢。
a shop near a bookstore「書店附近的一家店」。sugar（糖）、noise（噪音）、weather（天氣）都不是地點。
a nearby movie theater「附近的電影院」，幫忙貼海報。pumpkin（南瓜）、fever、sock 都不能和 movie 組成場所。

passages.zh: 在韓國和很多其他地方，K-pop 粉絲有一種特別的方式替偶像慶生：他們租下一間咖啡廳或小餐廳好幾天，用海報、照片和氣球布置，這叫做「生日咖啡廳」。來的粉絲買一杯飲料，就能拿到免費的杯套、貼紙和小卡。有些生日咖啡廳甚至和當地的麵包店合作，賣印有偶像臉的蛋糕。在台北，粉絲也會替柾國、智旻和子瑜等偶像辦生日咖啡廳，排隊人潮可以繞街區一圈。上個月，我朋友莉莉幫忙辦了一場柾國的生日咖啡廳。她在銀行存了半年的錢來支付費用，在一家書店附近的店印小卡，還請附近的電影院也貼一張海報。結果來了三百多位粉絲。莉莉說：「雖然很累，但看到大家的笑容，一切都值得了。」

passages.title: 湯裡有一隻蒼蠅
passages.text: My family went to a fancy {1} for my grandpa's birthday. Grandpa loves jokes. When the waiter brought his soup, Grandpa looked into the bowl and shouted, "Waiter! There's a fly in my soup!" Everyone in the {2} turned to look. The waiter looked carefully, then smiled. "Don't worry, sir. It's just a tiny piece of black pepper." Grandpa laughed and said, "Oh. Then why is it swimming?" The waiter laughed so hard that he almost dropped his tray. Of course, there was no fly. It really was pepper. Grandpa just wanted to tell his favorite old joke. After dinner, we went to a {3} to pick up his birthday cake, and he told the same joke to the baker. Then we walked past a {4}, and he went in to buy a joke book. "I need new jokes," he said. "The waiter has heard that one before." At home, he said he would keep the joke book safe, "like money in the {5}."

blanks.why: a fancy restaurant「一家高級餐廳」。spoon（湯匙）、cough（咳嗽）、fever（發燒）都不能慶生吃飯。
Everyone in the restaurant turned to look「餐廳裡每個人都轉頭看」。sock（襪子）、lemon（檸檬）、towel（毛巾）都不能容納客人。
went to a bakery to pick up the cake「去麵包店拿蛋糕」，後面說 baker。soup（湯）、blanket（毯子）、candle（蠟燭）都不是店。
walked past a bookstore and bought a joke book「經過書店買笑話書」。sugar（糖）、noise（噪音）、weather（天氣）都不賣書。
like money in the bank「像存在銀行的錢一樣」，比喻很安全。pumpkin（南瓜）、fever、sock 都不能讓錢變安全。

passages.zh: 我們全家去一家高級餐廳替爺爺慶生。爺爺很愛開玩笑。服務生把湯端上來時，爺爺看看碗裡，大喊：「服務生！我的湯裡有一隻蒼蠅！」餐廳裡每個人都轉頭看。服務生仔細看了看，笑著說：「先生別擔心，那只是一小片黑胡椒。」爺爺大笑：「喔，那它為什麼在游泳？」服務生笑到差點把托盤弄掉。當然，湯裡根本沒有蒼蠅，真的只是胡椒，爺爺只是想講他最愛的老笑話。吃完飯後，我們去麵包店拿生日蛋糕，他又對麵包師傅講了一次同樣的笑話。接著我們經過一家書店，他走進去買了一本笑話書。他說：「我需要新笑話，那個服務生以前聽過了。」回到家，他說他要把笑話書好好保管，「就像存在銀行裡的錢一樣」。

passages.title: 麵包店的早起比賽
passages.text: My uncle opened a small {1} across the street from another bakery. On the first day, the other baker put up a sign: "The best bread in town!" The next day, my uncle put up his own sign: "The best bread in the city!" The other baker got angry and put up a bigger sign: "The best bread in Taiwan!" Everyone on the street was watching to see what would happen next. On the third day, my uncle put up a tiny sign: "The best bread on this street." Customers laughed and lined up at his shop. The owner of the {2} next door even ordered 100 buns for lunch. The man from the {3} on the corner took a photo of the signs and posted it online, and it went viral. A week later, people from a local {4} group came to buy bread before their show. My uncle earned so much money that he had to visit the {5} every day. Now the two bakers are good friends, and they share a sign that says, "The best bread on both sides of the street."

blanks.why: opened a small bakery「開了一家小麵包店」，後面說另一家麵包店。spoon（湯匙）、cough（咳嗽）、fever（發燒）都不能開店。
the owner of the restaurant next door「隔壁餐廳的老闆」。sock（襪子）、lemon（檸檬）、towel（毛巾）都沒有老闆。
the man from the bookstore on the corner「轉角書店的老闆」。soup（湯）、blanket（毯子）、candle（蠟燭）都不是店。
a local theater group「當地的劇團」，表演前來買麵包。sugar（糖）、noise（噪音）、weather（天氣）都不能和 group 組成表演團體。
visit the bank every day「每天跑銀行」存錢。pumpkin（南瓜）、fever、sock 都不是地點。

passages.zh: 我舅舅在另一家麵包店的對街開了一家小麵包店。第一天，對面的麵包師傅掛出招牌：「全鎮最好吃的麵包！」隔天，舅舅也掛出自己的招牌：「全市最好吃的麵包！」對方很生氣，又掛了更大的招牌：「全台灣最好吃的麵包！」整條街的人都在看接下來會怎樣。第三天，舅舅掛出一個小小的招牌：「這條街上最好吃的麵包。」顧客都笑了，紛紛到他的店排隊。隔壁餐廳的老闆甚至訂了一百個麵包當午餐。轉角書店的老闆把招牌拍下來上傳到網路，結果爆紅了。一週後，當地一個劇團的人也在表演前來買麵包。舅舅賺了好多錢，每天都要跑銀行。現在兩位麵包師傅成了好朋友，一起掛了一塊招牌：「整條街兩邊最好吃的麵包。」

passages.title: 由劇院改建的書店
passages.text: In Buenos Aires, Argentina, there is a bookstore that many people call one of the most beautiful in the world. It's called El Ateneo Grand Splendid, and it used to be a {1}. The building opened in 1919 as the Teatro Grand Splendid, where people watched tango shows and concerts. Later, it became a movie {2}. In 2000, it was turned into a {3}, but the owners kept the painted ceiling, the red curtains, and the balconies. Today, shelves full of books stand where the seats used to be, and the old stage is now a café where people drink coffee and eat cake from a {4} nearby. About a million people visit it every year. My aunt went there on her trip to South America. She bought a small book of poems and sat in one of the old balconies to read it. She said she felt like the star of a show. When she came home, she told me she had spent so much on books that her {5} account was almost empty!

blanks.why: used to be a theater「以前是一座劇院」。spoon（湯匙）、cough（咳嗽）、fever（發燒）都不能讓人看表演。
became a movie theater「變成電影院」。sock（襪子）、lemon（檸檬）、towel（毛巾）都不能和 movie 組成場所。
turned into a bookstore「改建成書店」，後面說擺滿書的書架。soup（湯）、blanket（毯子）、candle（蠟燭）都不能賣書。
cake from a bakery nearby「附近麵包店的蛋糕」。sugar（糖）、noise（噪音）、weather（天氣）都不是店。
her bank account「她的銀行帳戶」。pumpkin（南瓜）、fever、sock 都不能和 account 組成存款帳戶。

passages.zh: 在阿根廷的布宜諾斯艾利斯，有一家被許多人稱為全世界最美的書店之一，叫做「雅典人書店」，它以前是一座劇院。這棟建築在 1919 年以「華麗大劇院」的名字開幕，大家在那裡看探戈表演和音樂會。後來它變成一家電影院。2000 年，它被改建成書店，但老闆保留了彩繪的天花板、紅色的布幕和包廂。今天，原本的座位區擺滿了書架，舊舞台變成了咖啡廳，大家在那裡喝咖啡、吃附近麵包店做的蛋糕。每年大約有一百萬人來參觀。我阿姨去南美洲旅行時去了那裡，她買了一本小詩集，坐在其中一個老包廂裡閱讀。她說自己就像表演的主角。回國後，她告訴我她買了太多書，銀行帳戶幾乎空了！

passages.title: 莎士比亞的環球劇場
passages.text: In the 1590s, William Shakespeare's plays were performed at the Globe, a round wooden {1} beside the River Thames in London. The first Globe burned down in 1613 during a play, and the second one was later closed. In 1997, a new Globe was built close to the old site, using the same kind of wood and the same round shape. Its thatched roof was the first one allowed in London since the Great Fire of 1666. Like the original, the center has no roof, so people who buy the cheapest tickets stand in the open air, rain or shine. Today, visitors from all over the world come to see Shakespeare's plays there. Nearby, there are many {2}, a small {3}, and a {4} that sells copies of his plays. Last summer, my English teacher stood there for three hours to watch Romeo and Juliet. She said her legs hurt, but it was worth every penny she took out of the {5}.

blanks.why: a round wooden theater「一座圓形的木造劇院」。spoon（湯匙）、cough（咳嗽）、fever（發燒）都不能演戲。
many restaurants「很多餐廳」。socks（襪子）、lemons（檸檬）、towels（毛巾）都不是附近的店家。
a small bakery「一家小麵包店」。soup（湯）、blanket（毯子）、candle（蠟燭）都不是店。
a bookstore that sells copies of his plays「一家賣他劇本的書店」。sugar（糖）、noise（噪音）、weather（天氣）都不賣書。
every penny she took out of the bank「她從銀行領出的每一分錢」。pumpkin（南瓜）、fever、sock 都不能領錢。

passages.zh: 1590 年代，莎士比亞的戲劇在環球劇場上演，那是一座位於倫敦泰晤士河畔的圓形木造劇院。第一座環球劇場在 1613 年演出時燒毀，第二座後來也關閉了。1997 年，人們在舊址附近蓋了一座新的環球劇場，用同樣的木材、同樣的圓形設計。它的茅草屋頂是 1666 年倫敦大火以來，倫敦第一座獲准使用茅草的屋頂。和原本的劇場一樣，中間沒有屋頂，所以買最便宜門票的人要站在露天的地方看戲，不論晴雨。今天，世界各地的遊客都來這裡看莎士比亞的戲。附近有很多餐廳、一家小麵包店，還有一家賣他劇本的書店。去年夏天，我的英文老師在那裡站了三個小時看《羅密歐與茱麗葉》。她說腿很痠，但從銀行領出的每一分錢都很值得。
